la:verb:remaneo.html:
rĕ-mănĕo, mansi, 2, v. n.,
to stay or remain behind (freq. and class.: cf. commoror).
In gen., absol.: ita sermone confecto, Catulus remansit, nos ad naviculas nostras descendimus,; (opp. discessus): qui per causam valetudinis remansit,: in castris Pompei,: cubito remanete presso,: quid fugis? O remane, (opp. deserere) et saep.: mulieres nostrae Romae remanserunt,: Romae,; : in exercitu,: in Galliā,: ad urbem cum imperio,: domi,: apud aliquem,fin.: ferrum ex hastili in corpore remanserat,: qui tam pauci remanserint,.—
In partic., to stay, remain, be left, continue, abide, endure: at manet in vitā, cui mens animusque remansit,; : expone igitur primum animos remanere post mortem,: equos eodem remanere vestigio adsuefaciunt,; cf.: vestigia antiqui officii remanent,; cf.: quorum usque ad nostram memoriam disciplina navalis et gloria remansit,: in duris remanentem rebus amicum,persevering, constant,: specie remanente coronae,: remanentes spicas,the remaining ears,: si ulla apud vos memoria remanet avi mei Masinissae,: id nomen (i. e. hostis) a peregrino recepit et proprie in eo, qui arma contra ferret, remansit,; : vobis aeterna sollicitudo remanebit,: ne quam contumeliam remanere in exercitu victore sinat,would suffer to cleave to the army,: ne quid ex contagione noxae remaneret penes nos,: quod est oratori necessarium, ab iis petere necesse est, apud quos remansit,: si quid antiqui remanet tibi vigoris,: ne qua materia seditionis remaneret,: solum se de cohorte Alexandri remansisse,.—
With an adjectival predicate, to remain, continue in a certain state or condition (cf. relinquo, I. B. 3.): quarum (sublicarum) pars inferior integra remanebat,: quae (potentia senatūs) gravis et magna remanebat,; : nec cognoscenda remansit Herculis effigies,.

la:verb:remitto.gloss: to send back, to remit, to throw back, restore
senses: to send back, to remit, to throw back, restore
to forgive, free one from any thing
to give up, reject, yield, resign, grant, concede
to omit to do any thing
la:verb:remitto.html:
rĕ-mitto, mīsi, missum, 3, v. a. and n.
Act., to let go back, send back, despatch back, drive back, cause to return (class. and very freq.; cf. reddo).
Lit.
In gen.: Al. Redde mihi illam (filiam) ... Non remissura es mihi illam? ... non remittes? Me. Non remittam! : a legione omnes remissi sunt domum Thebis,: aliquem domum,; ; fin.; : mulieres Romam,: paucos in regnum,: Fabium cum legione in sua hiberna,: partem legionum in sua castra,: ad parentes aliquem nuntium,: aliquem ad aliquem,; ; ; : obsides alicui,; Lucil. ap. : is argentum huc remisit,: librum tibi remisi,: pila intercepta, to cast or hurl back, ; so, tractum de corpore telum,: epistulam ad aliquem,: litteras Caesari,; cf.: scripta ad eum mandata per eos,: naves ad aliquem,; so, naves,: obsides,; : nonne vides etiam, quantā vi tigna trabesque Respuat umor aquae? .. Tam cupide sursum revomit magis atque remittit,drives back,; so, aquas longe (cautes),: calces (equi),i. e. kick out behind,.—
To send forth from itself, give out, yield: ut melius muriā, quam testa marina remittit,gives forth, yields,: muriam,: minimum seri,: umorem (humus),: aeruginem (vasa aenea),: nec umenti sensit tellure remitti (nebulas),: umorem ex se ipsa remittit,: quod baca remisit olivae,: sanguinem e pulmone,.—
In partic.
To let go back, to loosen, slacken, relax any thing strained, bound, rigid, etc. (syn. relaxo; opp. intendo, adduco): in agro ambulanti ramulum adductum, ut remissus esset, in oculum suum recidisse,; cf.: habenas vel adducere vel remittere,: frena, (opp. retinere); 6, 228: lora,; ; cf.: vela pennarum,: ira contractis, hilaritas remissis (superciliis) ostenditur,: quattuor remissis (digitis) magis quam tensis,: digitis,: remissis,: junctasque manus remisit; vinclis remissis, etc.,i. e. to loose, sq.: digitum contrahens ac remittens,: bracchia, i. e. to let sink or fall down, : remissas manus, sinking or failing, : frigore mella Cogit hiems eademque calor liquefacta remittit,dissolves again, melts,; cf.: cum se purpureo vere remittit humus,opens again, thaws,: vere remissus ager,. —
To leave behind, produce: veluti tractata notam labemque remittunt Atramenta,.—
Jurid. t. t.: remittere nuntium or repudium, to send a bill of divorce, to dissolve a marriage or betrothal; v. nuntius and repudium.—
Trop.
In gen., to send back, give back, return, restore, dismiss, remove, etc.: (specula) simulacra remittunt, Lachm.: vocem late nemora alta remittunt,; cf.: totidemque remisit Verba locus,: chorda sonum ... remittit acutum (with reddere),: vos me imperatoris nomine appellavistis: cujus si vos paenitet, vestrum vobis beneficium remitto, mihi meum restituite nomen,: quin etiam ipsis (imperium) remittere,: integram causam ad senatum remittit, refers, : a quibus appellatum erit, si forte ad eosdem remittemur,; : veniam,to return, repay,: quae nisi respuis ex animo longeque remittis,; cf.: opinionem animo,to dismiss, reject, cast off,: si quid ab omnibus conceditur, id reddo ac remitto,resign it,: utramque provinciam remitto, exercitum depono,: Galliam togatam,.—
In partic.
(Acc. to I A. 2. a.) To slacken, relax, relieve, release, abate, remit (freq. and class.): omnes sonorum tum intendens tum remittens persequetur gradus,; cf.: (sonorum vis) tum remittit animos, tum contrahit,: quaero enim non quibus intendam rebus animum, sed quibus relaxem ac remittam, relieve, recreate, refresh, id. Fragm. ap. : ut requiescerem curamque animi remitterem,: animum per dies festos licentius,; and in a like sense with se, ; and mid.: mirum est, ut opusculis animus intendatur remittaturque,: animos a contentione pugnae,: animos a certamine,: animos a religione,; cf.: nihil apud milites remittitur a summo certamine,: superioris temporis contentionem,; cf. : diligentiam in perdiscendo ac memoriam,; cf.: curam et diligentiam remittunt,: summum illud suum studium remisit,: ea studia remissa temporibus revocavi,: belli opera,: bellum,: pugnam,: urguent tamen et nihil remittunt,: equites petere ut sibi laxaret aliquid laboris; quibus ille, ne nihil remissum dicatis, remitto, etc.,: cottidie aliquid iracundiae remittebat,; cf. : aliquid de suo,: horam de meis legitimis horis,: aliquid de severitate cogendi,; : nihil de saevitiā,; cf. : ex eo, quod ipse potest in dicendo, aliquantum remittet,: aliquid ex pristinā virtute,: aliquid ex curā verborum,; .—With ellipsis of aliquid, etc.: illum viris fortissimis remittere de summā non potuisse, te mulieri deterrimae recte remississe, etc.,; : de voluntate nihil,: nihil e solito luxu,: nihil ex arrogantiā,— Impers.: tum aequo animo remittendum de celeritate existumabat,.—
With inf., to cease, leave off, omit to do any thing (rare; not in Cic. or Cæs.): si cogites, remittas jam me onerare injuriis,: neque remittit quid ubique hostis ageret explorare,; cf.: quid bellicosus Cantaber cogitet, remittas Quaerere,.—
With se, or mid., to relax, abate: ubi dolor et inflammatio se remiserunt,; cf.: cum se furor ille remisit,: quae (febres) certum habent circuitum et ex toto remittuntur,; cf. under II.—
Mid., to recreate one's self: eundem, cum scripsi, eundem etiam cum remittor, lego,; cf.: fas est et carmine remitti,; cf. supra: animus remittatur,.—(ε) To give free course to (opp. continere): animi appetitus, qui tum remitterentur, tum continerentur,.—
With respect to a person, to free one from any thing; to give up, grant, forgive, yield, resign, concede, surrender, sacrifice a thing to any one (= concedere, condonare); with acc. of the offence: Tranioni remitte quaeso hanc noxiam causā meā,: injuriam, Dietsch: quare tum cito senex ille remisit injuriam?: ut ex animo tibi volens omne delictum remittam,; so freq. in late Lat., to remit, forgive a sin or offence: peccata,: blasphemia,: cogitationem,. — Freq. with acc. of the penalty: multam,: poenam alicui,: ipso remittente Verginio ultimam poenam, ; : omnia tibi ista concedam et remittam,; cf. ; and: alicui remittere atque concedere, ut, etc.,: meam animadversionem et suppli cium ... remitto tibi et condono, Vatin. ap. : quod natura remittit, Invida jura negant,: si per populum Romanum stipendium remittatur,: pecunias, quas erant in publicum Varroni cives Romani polliciti, remittit,; cf. : aedes (venditas) alicui, to give up, resign a purchase, : tempus vobis,: ut patria tantum nobis in nostrum privatum usum, quantum ipsi superesse posset, remitteret,: navem imperare debuisti ex foedere: remisisti in triennium: militem nullum umquam poposcisti per tot annos,: tibi remittunt omnes istam voluptatem et eā se carere patiuntur,resign that pleasure to you,: ut memoriam simultatium patriae remitteret,sacrifice to his country,; cf.: privata odia publicis utilitatibus remittere,: ut sibi poenam magistri equitum remitteret (dictator),that he would remit for their sake,: dictator consulibus in senatu magnifice conlaudatis et suarum quoque rerum illis remisso honore, dictaturā se abdicavit,having been resigned in their favor,: jus ipsi remittent,will abandon their claim,.— Absol.: remittentibus tribunis plebis comitia per interregem sunt habita,withdrawing their opposition,: de tributo remiserunt,; cf. : si hoc ipsi remitti vellent, remitterent ipsi de maritumis custodiis,.—
Poet., with inf., to allow, permit: sed mora damnosa est nec res dubitare remittit,; cf.: (Fides) occulte saevire vetat, prodesse remittit,. —
Neutr., to decrease, abate (very rare, but class.): si forte ventus remisisset,: imbres,: pestilentia,: cum remiserant dolores pedum,; cf.: si remittent quippiam Philumenae dolores,: tumor remittens,: vapor calidus primo non remittit propter levitatem,does not sink,.— Hence, rĕmissus, a, um, P. a. (acc. to I. A. 2. a.), slack, loose, relaxed, languid (opp. contentus, contendere): membra,.
Lit.: ut onera contentis corporibus facilius feruntur, remissis opprimunt,; cf.: vox, ut nervi, quo remissior, hoc gravior et plenior,: ridens Venus et remisso Filius arcu,: ammoniacum,i. e. liquid,; cf. adeps,. —
Trop., relaxed, not rigid, strict, or hard, both in a good and bad sense.
Mild, gentle, soft, indulgent, cheerful, good-humored, gay, etc. (syn.: lenis, mitis, dulcis): remissior ventus,: remissiora frigora,: cantūs remissiores,; cf.: tum intentis tum remissis modis,: si me non improbissime Dolabella tractasset, dubitassem fortasse, utrum remissior essem, an summo jure contenderem,: in eo sermone non remissi sumus,: remissus et subridens,: nisi magistratus valde lenes et remissi sint,: in ulciscendo remissior,: animus (with lenis),; cf.: remississimo ad otium et ad omnem comitatem animo,i. e. most prone,: remissus et mitis,: cum tristibus severe, cum remissis jucunde vivere,; cf. ; : decorus est sermo senis quietus et remissus,: remissius genus dicendi,: amicitia remissior esse debet et liberior et dulcior,; cf. affectus,: egressiones dulces et remissae,: joci, gay, merry (opp. curae graves), ; cf.: remissiores hilarioresque sermones,: opus,. —
Slack, negligent, remiss (syn. languidus): esse remisso ac languido animo,; cf.: nostris languentibus atque animo remissis,: dolus Numidarum

nihil languidi neque remissi patiebatur, i. e. no negligence, ; : in labore,: oderunt agilem gnavumque remissi,: remissior in petendo,: vita remissior,.—

Lower, cheaper: remissior aliquanto ejus fuit aestimatio quam annona,below the market price,. — Hence, adv.: rĕ-missē (acc. to B. 1.), gently, mildly (with leniter, urbane; opp. severe, graviter, vehementer, etc.),; ; ; ; ; .—Comp., ; ; .—Sup. is not found.

la:noun:remedium.html:
rĕmĕdĭum, ii, n.
re-medeor
,
that which heals again; a cure, remedy (class. and freq.).
Lit., a remedy, medicine: ratio remedi certa,: pantheras, quae in barbariā venenatā carne caperentur, remedium quoddam habere, quo cum essent usae, non morerentur,: contrariis remediis sanant,.—With gen.: remedium est magni et recentis doloris sanguis missus,.—With contra: contra omnium morsus remedio est gallinaceum cerebrum,: fumum ejus contra alia ligna,; .— Absol.: abstinere cibo omni, aut potu, etc.... in praesentissimis remediis habetur,: in remedio est,: remedium ad fauces pollicitus, et saep.—
Esp., a charm, amulet, magic preventive: si qui remedia quartanae vel doloris alterius collo gestaret,.—
Trop., a means of aid, assistance, or relief; a remedy: ad magnitudinem frigorum remedium comparare,; so, remedia sibi comparare ad tolerandum dolorem,: remedium quaerere ad moram,; cf.: adversus consulta senatūs et decreta principum vel magistratuum remedium nullum est, nisi, etc.,: adversus reliqua uti remediis,: remedium in ceteros,: illius tanti vulneris,: aegritudinum,: miseriarum,: iracundiae,: infirmae memoriae,: hujus metūs,: ubertatis,: cum hoc unum his tot in commodis remedium esse arbitrarer,: quibus rebus nostri haec reperiebant remedia, ut, etc., Caes B. C. 3, 50; cf.: veneficiis remedia invenire,: quod remedium huic malo inveniam?; id. Phorm, 1, 4, 23; 4, 3, 11: acrioribus saluti suae remediis subvenire,: id remedium timori fuit,: cum utrumque ipsi pro remedio aegris rebus discordiā intestinā petissent,: hinc ira et questus, et postquam non subinveniebat (Olennius) remedium ex bello,.

la:noun:remus.html:
rēmus, i, m.
ἐρετμός
,
an oar.
Lit., : ut retinet navis cursum, intermisso impetu pulsuque remorum,; : remis navem incitare,; 4, 25: remis contendere,; ; ; ; : incumbere remis,: remis insurgere,; 560: inpellere aequora remis,.—Prov.: remis velisque, velis remisque, remis ventisque; also, ventis remis, with sails and oars, i. e. with all one's might, with all possible speed: ita citi remis velisque impellite puppim,: res omni contentione, velis, ut ita dicam, remisque fugienda,: laevam cuncta cohors remis ventisque petivit,: inde ventis remis in patriam omni festinatione properavi, (cf.: remigio veloque festinare,).—
Poet., transf., of the wings of birds: alarum,: pennarum (Icari),.— Of the hands and feet of a swimmer,.—
Trop.: quaerebam, utrum panderem vela orationis statim, an eam ante paululum dialecticorum remis propellerem, (shortly before, remigare; opp. vela facere).

la:noun:remex.html:
rēmex, ĭgis (
gen. plur. remigium, ), m.
remus-ago
, a rower, oarsman, . 35; ; ; ; ; ; ; .—Poet., of Charon, .—Of the fish that swallowed Jonah: remige inimico,.—
Remex, collect. for remiges, a bench of rowers, the oarsmen of a vessel (poet. and postAug.): vacuos sensit sine remige portus,: Velocem Mnestheus agit acri remige Pristim,; (4, 11), 34; ; ; ; : non remigem, non socios navalis ad classem frequentis habiturum,; : remex militis officia turbabat, : milite ac remige,; .

la:verb:remigo.html:
rēmĭgo, āre, v. n.
id.
,
to row (class.), : utrum mavis? statimne vela facere, an paululum remigare?: non intermisso remigandi labore,; Auct. B. Alex. 46, 2; ; : contra aquam,—Poet., with acc.: remigare alnum (i. e. navem),.

la:verb:removeo.html:
rĕ-mŏvĕo, mōvi, mōtum, 2 (sync.
pluperf. remorant, ; ; inf. remosse, ; perf. remorunt, ), v. a., to move back, draw back; to take away, set aside, withdraw, remove (freq. and class.; syn.: amolior, repono, segrego).
Lit.: tolle hanc patinam, remove pernam,: pecora,: equos,: equos ex conspectu,: dapes,: mensam,: frena, Hor.S.2, 7, 74: tegimen,to lay aside,: Aurora removerat ignes,had driven away,: monstra,: remoto atque ablegato viro,: remotis arbitris,: custode remoto,: remoto Hannibale,: quae jam infantem removerit,i. e. has weaned,: naves longas ab onerariis navibus,: cupas furcis ab opere,: castra sex milia ab oppido,: quae natura occultavit ab oculis,: bracchia a latere modice,: comas a fronte ad aures,: se a corpore,: se a vulgo,: parvos natos a se,: se a conspectu, Auct. B. Afr. 62: plura de medio (with auferre),: togam inde,: oculos,: arcanis oculos profanos,: tactu viriles virgineo manus,: toto sumus orbe remoti,: mensae remotae, ; : cum paulum ab legionibus nostros removissent,: aliquem ab exercitu, Auct. B. Afr. 54: praesidia ex iis locis, quae, etc.,: se in montes ex urbe,: ex oculis manus,: ut propinquis suis ultra ducentesimum lapidem removeretur,.—
Trop.: removete moram,; , prooem. § 3;: sumptum removit,: hominum conscientiā remotā,: remotā subtilitate disputandi,: omnia removistis, avaritiam, imperitiam, superbiam,; cf.: remoto metu,; : remoto joco,jesting aside,: remoto personarum complexu,; : formam anilem,: soporem,: obstantia fata,: remove istaec, no more of that (i. e. do not speak of it), Cic. ap. : aliquem ab studio, prol. alt. 14: aliquem ab republicā,; : aliquem ab hoc sermone,: aliquem a legibus (sc. ferendis),: aliquem a vitā (natura),: se a negotiis publicis,: se ab omni ejusmodi negotio,: se ab amicitiā alicujus,; cf.: se ab aliquo,, b, 3: se a suspitione,; cf.: illam suspitionem ab sese removere,: invidiam a se,: vim procul hinc,: (levissima) secerni arbitror oportere atque ex oratione removeri,: quartum (statum) ex generalibus,: omnes tribu remoti, Drak. N. cr.: ordine,: quaesturā,: pudorem thalamis,; cf.: se artibus suis,: se ministerio sceleris,: aliquem tutelā,.— Absol., . —
To deduct, subtract: si de quincunce remota est Uncia,.—Hence, rĕmōtus, a, um, P. a., removed, i. e. afar off, distant, remote.
Lit.: silvestribus ac remotis locis,distant, retired,; cf.: remoto loco,: terrae,: Gades,: Britanni,: fontes,: gramen,: rupes,: domūs pars, i. e. penetralia,. —Neutr. as subst.: in remoto,far away,: remotius antrum,: sedes, remotas a Germanis,: ab arbitris remoto loco,: civitas a conspectu remota,, § 85: in quibus (studiis) remoti ab oculis populi omne otiosum tempus contrivimus,: ab aulā,.— With abl.: civitatis oculis remotus,: quamvis longā regione remotus Absim,by however great a distance I am removed from you,; cf.: licet caeli regione remotus,.—
Trop., removed, disconnected, separate, clear, free from, strange to any thing: quae jam diu gesta et a memoriā remota,: genus (narrationum) remotum a civilibus causis,: natura deūm longe remota Sensibus ab nostris,: scientia remota ab justitiā,: (defensio) remota ab utilitate rei publicae,: a verā ratione longe remotum,: (fabula) non a veritate modo, sed etiam a formā veritatis remota,: naturae jura a vulgari intellegentiā remotiora,: sermo a forensi strepitu remotissimus,; Spald. N. cr.: (Vestorium) hominem remotum a dialecticis, in arithmeticis satis versatum,: homines maxime ab injuriis nostrorum magistratuum remoti,: a Tib. Gracchi aequitate ac pudore longissime remotus,: hic a culpā est remotus,: ab inani laude et sermonibus vulgi,: a vulgo longe lateque,: vitio ab omni,: ab omni minimi errati suspicione remotissimus,: (vilica) a vino, ab escis, a superstitionibus remotissima sit, et saep.—
In the philos. lang. of the Stoics, remota, a transl. of the Gr. προηγμένα,things not to be preferred;

things to be rejected

 or postponed (opp. promota), .—Hence, adv.: rĕmōtē, at a distance, afar off, remotely (very rare).—Comp.: stellae eundem orbem tenentes aliae propius a terris, aliae remotius ab eisdem principiis eadem spatia conficiunt,.— Sup.: remotissime,.

la:adj:remissior.html:
rĕmissĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
(acc. to remitto, I. A. and B.),
a sending back or away, releasing
Lit. (rare).
A sending back, returning; of persons: obsidum captivorumque,.—Of things, a throwing back, reflecting: splendoris,.—
A letting down, lowering: ex superciliorum aut remissione aut contractione,.—
Trop.
A slackening, relaxing, abating, diminishing, remitting; remission, relaxation, abatement (syn. relaxatio): animus intentione suā depellit pressum omnem ponderum, remissione autem sic urgetur, ut se nequeat extollere,: contentiones vocis et remissiones,; cf. ; so, vocis,: σφυγμὸς est intentio motūs et remissio in corde et in arteria, : remissio lenitatis quādam gravitate et contentione firmatur,laxity,: operis,; cf. laboris,; : tales igitur amicitiae sunt remissione usus eluendae,: senescentis morbi remissio,; so, febris,: doloris,.—
Slackness, laxness, want of spirit: in acerbissimā injuriā remissio animi ac dissolutio,.—
Relaxation, recreation: ad omnem animi remissionem ludumque descendere,; so, animorum,; .—Absol.: quem non quies, non remissio, non aequalium studia, non ludi delectarent,: danda est omnibus aliqua remissio,.—Absol. in plur., ; ; , : tempora curarum remissionumque,; .—
Mildness, gentleness, lenity: (Adversarius) tum ad severitatem, tum ad remissionem animi est contorquen dus, (cf. remissus, B. 1.): so, remissione poenae,by a relaxing, diminishing of punishment, by a milder punishment,.—
(Acc. to remitto, I. B. 2. b.) A remitting of a penalty, etc., a remission, ; ; ; : remissio tributi in triennium,: nuntiationis,remission, abrogation,.— Plur.: post magnas remissiones,reduction of rent,.—
In eccl. Lat., remission, forgiveness of sin, etc.: delicti,: peccatorum, Ambros. de Isaac et Anim. 1, 1; ; .— *
A repetition: nova ludorum remissio,.

la:verb:reminiscor.html:
rĕ-mĭniscor, sci,
v. dep. n. and a. [root men; whence mens, memini; v. comminiscor].
To recall to mind, recollect, remember (syn. recordor): reminisci, quom ea quae tenuit mens ac memoria, cogitando repetuntur, Müll.: se non tum illa discere, sed reminiscendo recognoscere,; cf. : te de aliis quibusdam quaestoribus reminiscentem recordari,.— With gen.: reminisceretur veteris incommodi populi Romani, * : veteris famae,: Satyri,: facti,: reminiscere quae traduntur mysteriis,. — With acc.: ea potius reminiscere, quae, etc., Sulp. ap. : acerbitatem pristini temporis,: dulces Argos,: animo dulces amicos,: tempus illud,: acta,; .—With obj.-clause: reminiscere, totius imum Nil esse in summā,, 90; 6, 649; ; cf. . —With rel.-clause: reminiscerentur quam majestatem accepissent,; .—
To call to mind, imagine, conceive: ut, si ipse fingere vellet, neque plura bona reminisci, neque majora posset consequi, quam vel fortuna vel natura tribuerat, dub. (al. comminisci): reminiscimini quod respondeatis,: finge quidvis, reminiscere, excogita, quid possit magicum videri, p. 308, 33.?*! Act. collat. form rĕmĭnisco, ĕre, acc. to P.; censured by and 49.

la:verb:remigro.html:
rĕ-mī^gro, āre, v. n.,
to remove or journey back; to go back, return (class.).
Lit.: facere ut remigret domum,; cf.: in domum suam,: in domum veterem e novā,: in locum,. trans Rhenum in suos vicos, . 4: in agros,fin.: Romam,.— Absol.: subitum est ei remigrare Kalendis Quintilibus,.—
Trop.: ad argumentum,: ad justitiam,: ad deos (anima sapientis),. remigrat animus nunc demum mihi, .

la:noun:remissio.html:
rĕmissĭo, ōnis, f.
id.
(acc. to remitto, I. A. and B.),
a sending back or away, releasing
Lit. (rare).
A sending back, returning; of persons: obsidum captivorumque,.—Of things, a throwing back, reflecting: splendoris,.—
A letting down, lowering: ex superciliorum aut remissione aut contractione,.—
Trop.
A slackening, relaxing, abating, diminishing, remitting; remission, relaxation, abatement (syn. relaxatio): animus intentione suā depellit pressum omnem ponderum, remissione autem sic urgetur, ut se nequeat extollere,: contentiones vocis et remissiones,; cf. ; so, vocis,: σφυγμὸς est intentio motūs et remissio in corde et in arteria, : remissio lenitatis quādam gravitate et contentione firmatur,laxity,: operis,; cf. laboris,; : tales igitur amicitiae sunt remissione usus eluendae,: senescentis morbi remissio,; so, febris,: doloris,.—
Slackness, laxness, want of spirit: in acerbissimā injuriā remissio animi ac dissolutio,.—
Relaxation, recreation: ad omnem animi remissionem ludumque descendere,; so, animorum,; .—Absol.: quem non quies, non remissio, non aequalium studia, non ludi delectarent,: danda est omnibus aliqua remissio,.—Absol. in plur., ; ; , : tempora curarum remissionumque,; .—
Mildness, gentleness, lenity: (Adversarius) tum ad severitatem, tum ad remissionem animi est contorquen dus, (cf. remissus, B. 1.): so, remissione poenae,by a relaxing, diminishing of punishment, by a milder punishment,.—
(Acc. to remitto, I. B. 2. b.) A remitting of a penalty, etc., a remission, ; ; ; : remissio tributi in triennium,: nuntiationis,remission, abrogation,.— Plur.: post magnas remissiones,reduction of rent,.—
In eccl. Lat., remission, forgiveness of sin, etc.: delicti,: peccatorum, Ambros. de Isaac et Anim. 1, 1; ; .— *
A repetition: nova ludorum remissio,.

la:other:Remi.gloss: A tribe of Gallia Belgica whose chief town was Durocortorum
senses: A tribe of Gallia Belgica whose chief town was Durocortorum
la:other:Remi.html:
Rēmi (Rhēmi), ōrum, m.
A considerable people of Gaul, in the region round about the modern Rheims, ; sq.; 9; 12; 3, 11; 5, 3 et saep.; —In sing.: Iccius Remus,.—Poet., collect., .—
In later authors, the chief town of the Remi, now Rheims (in earlier writers, Durocortorum; cf. ), ; .

la:verb:remordeo.html:
rĕ-mordeo, no
perf., rsum, 2, v. a., to bite again; mostly poet., and only in the trop. sense; to vex, torment, disturb: me remorsurum petis,: praeteritis male admissis peccata remordent,: animus se forte remordet,: quando haec te cura remordet,; cf. absol.: si juris materni cura remordet,: vitia castigata remordent, Juy. 2. 25.—In prose: sin tandem libertatis desiderium remordet animos, .

senses: the equipment, fittings and people used in rowing
la:noun:remigium.html:
rēmĭgĭum, ii, n.
remex
.
Lit., a rowing: homines remigio sequi,: olli remigio noctemque diemque fatigant,: portus decem dierum remigio ab oppido distans (just before: abest a Ptolemaide quinque dierum navigatione),; .—
Meton. (abstr. pro concreto).
The parts of a vessel that belong to the rowing of it, the oars, ; ; Hor C. 1, 14, 4; ; ; .—Prov.: remigio veloque festinare,i. e. with all possible speed, (cf.: remis velisque; v. 1. remus, I. A.): meo remigio rem gero,i. e. I steer my own course, do just as I please, (v. l. meo remigio remigo; cf. Brix ad loc.).—
Poet., of wings: remigi oblitae (aves),: volat ille per aëra magnum Remigio alarum,; (mentioned in ); ; : (aquila) remigium dextrā laevāque porrigens, (cf. in the Gr. Aesch. Agam. 52: πτερύγων ἐρετμοῖσιν ἐρεσσόμενοι).—
Those that perform the rowing, the oarsmen, rowers, : remigium classicique milites, tranquillo in altum evecti,; ; ; 33, 48; 37, 11; ; : remigium vitiosum Ulixei,.

la:verb:remeo.gloss: to go back, come back, return
senses: to go back, come back, return
la:verb:remeo.html:
rĕ-mĕo, āvi, 1, v. n.,
to go or come back, to turn back, return (not freq. till after the

Aug. period; only once in Cic.; in Cæs. not at all; syn.: redeo, regredior).

Lit.: remeabo intro,: remeato audacter,: in ludum, Afr. ap. Fest. s. h. v. p. 277 Müll. (Com. Rel. p. 151 Rib.): in patriam,: patrias in sedes,: rursum in terga (with cedere),: ad se (legati),: ex Campaniā,; cf. Aegypto,: eodem remeante nuntio,: navibus remeabat disjecto agmine,; cf. Plin. fin.: (coturnices) cum ex Italiā trans mare remeant,: greges nocte remeabant ad stabula,; . —
Poet. and late Lat. with acc.: patrias remeabo inglorius urbes,: Euboicos penates,: destinatas remeārunt sedes,: castra, pr.—
Of inanimate subjects: cum umore consumpto neque terra ali posset neque remearet aër, would flow back again, * : (naves) mari remeabant,: remeante flumine,receding,: bis adfluunt bisque remeant (aquae),.—
In partic., to come back as a victor, return home in triumph (poet.; cf. Cort. ad ; Burm. ad ): victor ad Argos,; cf.: victor domito ab hoste,: Scythicis Crassus victor ab oris,: nunc neque te longi remeantem pompa triumphi Excipit,: triumpho,.—With acc.: vetitos remeare triumphos, to return home to the triumph denied (me), .—
Trop., to come back, return: transiit aetas, Quam cito, non segnis stat remeatque dies,.—With acc.: si natura juberet A certis annis aevom remeare peractum,.—In discourse: ad ordinem remeabo coeptorum,?*! Lengthened collat. form remānant = remeant (like dănunt = dant, prodīnunt = prodeunt, redīnunt = redeunt): rivos camposque remanant, Enn. Fragm. ap. Müll. (Ann. v. 72 Vahl.).

la:verb:remensus.html: rĕmensus, a, um, Part., v. remetior, I. A. and B.

la:other:Remus.html:
rēmus, i, m.
ἐρετμός
,
an oar.
Lit., : ut retinet navis cursum, intermisso impetu pulsuque remorum,; : remis navem incitare,; 4, 25: remis contendere,; ; ; ; : incumbere remis,: remis insurgere,; 560: inpellere aequora remis,.—Prov.: remis velisque, velis remisque, remis ventisque; also, ventis remis, with sails and oars, i. e. with all one's might, with all possible speed: ita citi remis velisque impellite puppim,: res omni contentione, velis, ut ita dicam, remisque fugienda,: laevam cuncta cohors remis ventisque petivit,: inde ventis remis in patriam omni festinatione properavi, (cf.: remigio veloque festinare,).—
Poet., transf., of the wings of birds: alarum,: pennarum (Icari),.— Of the hands and feet of a swimmer,.—
Trop.: quaerebam, utrum panderem vela orationis statim, an eam ante paululum dialecticorum remis propellerem, (shortly before, remigare; opp. vela facere).

senses: to go, pass or travel over again
la:verb:remetior.html:
rĕ-mētĭor, mensus, 4,
v. dep. a., to measure or mete again, measure or mete back (poet. and in post-Aug. prose).
Lit.: iter retro remensumst,: si modo rite memor servata remetior astra,: frumentum pecuniā remetiri, to measure back with money, i. e. to pay for with an equal measure of money, —In pass. sense: in quā mensurā mensi fueritis, remetietur,; .—
Transf.
To measure back, i. e. to go, pass, or travel over again: iter,: stadia,.— In pass. sense: pelagoque remenso, Improvisi aderunt,: remenso mari,.—
In gen., to void or discharge back again: ille fide summā testae sua vina remensus, Reddidit oenophori pondera plena sui,: vinum omne vomitu,; cf. .—
Trop., to go over in one's mind; to think over, reflect upon; to tell again, repeat: totum diem mecum scrutor, facta ac dicta mea remetior,: fabulam,; , p. 123, 35.—
(Acc. to I. B. 1.) To measure or pass over again: transmissum discrimen convalescendo remetiri, to remeasure, in recovering, the danger surmounted (i. e. to be continually advancing in recovery), .

senses: to moo or bellow in return
la:verb:remugio.html:
rĕ-mūgĭo, īre, v. n.,
to bellow back; to resound, re-echo (poet.): ad mea verba remugis,: Sibylla antro remugit,: totus remugit Mons,: Ionius remugiens sinus Noto,: nemus ventis,: gemitu nemus,: nemus alio bellatore (i. e. tauro),: nemus latratu,; cf.: vox assensu nemornm ingeminata remugit,: sequitur clamor caelumque remugit,: leve tympanum remugit,.

Lit.: caudam,i. e. to droop,: aures,to stroke gently,: crines,.—

la:verb:remoror.html:
rĕ-mŏror, ātus, 1,
v. dep. n. and a.
Neutr., to stay, tarry, linger, loiter, delay (so rarely): nam quid illaec nunc tam diu intus remorantur remeligines?: ibi corpora,: res nulla foris,: in concilio,; cf.: in Italiā,: sed postquam remorata suos cognovit amores,: perge, ne remorare. Non diu remoratus es: Jam venis,: Etesiae contra fluvium flantes remorantur,.—
Act., to hold back, stay, detain, obstruct, hinder, delay, defer (syn. retardare; freq. and class.): aliquem,: haec edepol remorata med est,; et saep.: di illum perdant, qui me hodie remoratus est,: eae res, quae ceteros remorari solent, non retardarunt,: nox atque praeda castrorum hostes quominus victoriā uterentur remorata sunt,; : quamvis te longae remorentur fata senectae,i. e. should preserve you to a good old age,: num unum diem postea L. Saturninum tribunum plebis et C. Servilium praetorem mors ac poena remorata est?i. e. was it put off, deferred?; cf. : cur non remoratur ituros,.—Absol.: ab negotiis numquam voluptas remorata,.—With inanimate and abstract objects: alicujus commodum,: scio te me iis epistulis potius et meas spes solitum esse remorari,: alicujus iter,; so, iter,.—Absol.: fugiunt, freno non remorante, dies,.?*! rĕmŏrātus, a, um, in a pass. signif.: remorandust gradus,: pomi jactu remorata (Atalanta),.

la:noun:remulcum.html:
rĕmulcum (rymulcum, acc. to the Gr., ), i (for the most part only in abl.), n.
ῥυμουλκέω
, nautical t. t.,
a tow-rope, or any other contrivance for towing: remulcum funis, quo deligata navis magnā trahitur vice remi,: remulco est, cum scaphae remis navis magna trahitur, Müll.: navem remulco abstraxit,: submersam navim remulco adduxit,: naves onerarias remulco Alexandriam deducit, Auct. B. Alex. 11 fin.: navem remulco trahere,; . — Here prob. belongs the fragment of Sisenna: in altum remulco trahit, Sisenn. ap. (where Nonius erroneously assumes a verb, remulco, āre; cf. supra, the article of Festus, where also remulco forms the heading); Valgius ap. Isid. l. l.; ; ; . —Prov.: non contis nec rymulco, ut aiunt, sed velificatione plenā in rempublicam ferebantur,.

la:verb:remollesco.gloss: to become soft or soften again
senses: to become soft or soften again
la:verb:remollesco.html:
rĕ-mollesco, ĕre,
v. inch. n., to become soft again, to become or grow soft (class.).
Lit.: ut Hymettia sole Cera remollescit,softens,: sole remollescit quae frigore constitit unda,i. e. melts,.—
Trop.: quod ea re (vino) ad laborem ferendum remollescere homines atque effeminari arbitrantur, to be enervated, * : si precibus numina justis Victa remollescunt,are softened, touched,.

la:noun:remora.html:
rĕ-mŏra, ae, f.,
delay, hinderance, passive resistance (ante- and post-class.): quae Remoram faciunt rei privatae et publicae,; cf. Lucil. ap. Paul. ex Müll.: remora si sit,if I delay,: remorā ausus miserabiles casus levare multorum, (but in , the correct read. is mora).

remaneo
,
